script: I thought my mom was redeemed, until she got arrested—shocking truth revealed.. My mom got arrested for domestic violence against an 8‑year‑old yesterday. I'd finally let her back in two years after cutting her off for the shit she'd done to me and my siblings. She'd remarried, looked all "improved" on the surface, and I was like, "Okay, Mom, welcome back." But the old her never really left. I'd just been ignoring it, happy to have a "healthy" relationship again. Then my 14‑year‑old brother died a month ago from lifelong medical issues. The cracks widened. I was still wearing rose‑colored glasses, but that all flipped when I got the call from my other brother. He'd been visiting her new girlfriend and their kid. They saw her drag my step‑sibling, who was 8, across the living‑room carpet—like a bad movie scene. He ran outside scared, but she chased him, dragged him across the road, into the front lawn. Neighbors started watching. She wrapped her whole body around him, a "bear hug" that stopped him from moving. Thankfully my brother was there. He called the cops and her husband. Mom was taken to the station and charged with domestic violence. She kept blaming everyone but herself. I hadn't felt that relief in so long. Remember when I was 17 and reported her to the school counselor for holding scissors to my sister's throat? I shoved between them, stopped her arm from going to her neck. I packed a bag, ran to a friend's place, and later found out she was arrested at work. Now she's sick. Part of me hopes she gets help. Another part? I want her to feel the same pain she inflicted. I know it's dark, so I am dumping it here. That's just a drop in the bucket of everything that happened growing up. I am glad she's finally caught. Maybe she won't hurt anyone else. I know my family will find this post later and ask why I'd share it. I don't care. I am an adult. I won't let her fear, retaliation, or family judgment haunt me anymore.
